title: The Continuum Hypothesis: Is there a cardinality between countable and continuum

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: Formal proof built and verified via Docker. Beth number hierarchy, CH ↔ no intermediate cardinal, König constraint all formalized. 1 sorry remaining (beth_unbounded).
builtItems: CantorDiagonalizationOQ01.lean: beth : ℕ → Cardinal.{0} (beth number hierarchy)
insights: The diagonal argument proves ℵ₀ < 2^ℵ₀ (beth₁) but cannot determine whether intermediate cardinals exist
CH ↔ no cardinal between ℵ₀ and 2^ℵ₀ - proved as clean equivalence using le_antisymm
Beth number hierarchy: beth_n < beth_{n+1} via Cardinal.cantor applied iteratively
Under ¬CH, ℵ₁ is itself an explicit intermediate cardinal: ℵ₀ < ℵ₁ < 2^ℵ₀
König's constraint: cf(2^ℵ₀) > ℵ₀, so 2^ℵ₀ cannot be ℵ_ω or any singular aleph
ℵ₁ = Order.succ ℵ₀ and ℵ₁ ≤ 2^ℵ₀ by Order.succ_le_of_lt + Cardinal.cantor
Universe pinning to Cardinal.{0} required throughout to avoid metavariable errors
mathlibGaps: König's cofinality theorem (cf(2^ℵ₀) > ℵ₀) axiomatized - would need Cardinal.IsRegular machinery
Cofinality of ℵ_ω = ω axiomatized - needs detailed Ordinal.cof computation
